questions.question:
What will come in the place of the question mark ‘(?)’ in the following equation, if ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?

57 ÷ 9 × 50 − 5 + 2 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2381f95ecfcbe7f6eaceba831d02f99bf624c84151895e65ac4d5a630f47ff34.png] 

Given interchange rules:

__
 
• ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged.
 
• ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged.

The given equation is:

57 ÷ 9 × 50 − 5 + 2 = ?

Replace the operators with their corresponding new meanings:

57 − 9 + 50 ÷ 5 × 2 = ?

Now, we solve the equation following the BODMAS rule:

= 57 − 9 + **50 ÷ 5**__ × 2

= 57 − 9 + __**10 × 2**__

= __**57 **__− 9 __**+ 20**__

= **__77 - 9__** = 68

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: Who founded the Kanva dynasty after the death of the last Shunga ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vasudeva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kanva dynasty was established by **Vasudeva**, who was a minister in the court of the last Shunga ruler, Devabhuti.
 
• Vasudeva is credited with overthrowing the Shunga dynasty and establishing the **Kanva rule around 73 BCE**.
 
• The Kanvas ruled from **73 BCE to 28 BCE** and were considered successors of the Shungas in the Magadha region.
 
• The Kanvas, like their predecessors, were **Brahmanical rulers** and continued to uphold Vedic traditions.
 
• The Kanva dynasty was ultimately defeated by the **Satavahanas**, marking the end of their rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shunga Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Shunga dynasty preceded the Kanvas and was founded by **Pushyamitra Shunga** after the fall of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• It lasted from around **185 BCE to 73 BCE** and was marked by the revival of Brahmanical traditions.
 
 
 
• **Transition to Kanva Rule:**
 
 
• The last Shunga ruler, **Devabhuti**, was known for his weak leadership, leading to his assassination by Vasudeva.
 
• The Kanva dynasty emerged as a short-lived but significant successor to the Shungas.
 
 
 
• **Satavahana Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Satavahanas were a prominent South Indian dynasty that eventually overthrew the Kanvas.
 
• They are credited with re-establishing political stability in the Deccan region after the fall of the Kanvas.
 
 
 
• **Magadha:**
 
 
• Magadha served as the central region of power for successive dynasties, including the Mauryas, Shungas, and Kanvas.
 
• It remained a significant political and cultural hub in ancient India.

questions.question: Who among the following authorities acts as the Vice Chairman of the Concerned Zonal council on rotation basis for a period of one year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Minister of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established under the States Reorganization Act of 1956 to foster cooperation and coordination between states.
 
• Each Zonal Council is chaired by the Union Home Minister, while the Chief Minister of the state acts as the Vice Chairman on a rotational basis for one year.
 
• The rotation of Vice Chairmanship ensures equal representation of states within the concerned zone.
 
• There are five Zonal Councils in India: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, and Southern, with each covering specific states and union territories.
 
• The Vice Chairman plays a key role in facilitating dialogue among member states to resolve inter-state issues and promote regional development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zonal Councils**

 
 
• These councils were created under Part III of the States Reorganization Act, 1956.
 
• The councils aim to resolve disputes, facilitate communication, and ensure balanced socio-economic development across states.
 
• They are advisory in nature and do not have legislative or executive powers.
 
 
 
• **Inter-State Council**
 
 
• It is a constitutional body established under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The council aims to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between states and the center.
 
• Unlike Zonal Councils, it addresses broader issues affecting multiple states across India.
 
 
 
• **Union Home Minister's Role**
 
 
• The Union Home Minister serves as the Chairman of all Zonal Councils.
 
• As Chairman, the Home Minister ensures coordination between states and the central government.
 
 
 
• **States Reorganization Act, 1956**
 
 
• This act was responsible for the linguistic reorganization of states in India.
 
• It also led to the creation of Zonal Councils as a mechanism for fostering cooperation among states.

questions.question: When an object is moving with constant speed in a straight line, its acceleration:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
 
• When an object is moving with constant speed in a straight line, its velocity remains unchanged over time.
 
• Since there is no change in velocity, the acceleration of the object is **zero**.
 
• Constant speed and straight-line motion imply no external force is causing a change in the object's velocity.
 
• This aligns with Newton's First Law of Motion, which states that an object will remain in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Velocity:** It is a vector quantity that describes the speed of an object in a specific direction.
 
• **Acceleration:** The rate at which an object’s velocity changes, calculated using the formula: *a = Δv / Δt*, where *Δv* is the change in velocity and *Δt* is the change in time.
 
• **Newton’s First Law:** An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion at constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force.
 
• **Uniform Motion:** When an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time without changing its speed or direction.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion:** When an object’s speed or direction changes, resulting in non-zero acceleration.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Prarthana Samaj, which promoted social reform in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmaram Pandurang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atmaram Pandurang was the **founder of the Prarthana Samaj**, established in 1867 in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the **Brahmo Samaj**, which advocated social and religious reform.
 
• It aimed to promote **social reforms**, such as the abolition of caste discrimination and child marriage, and encourage widow remarriage.
 
• Atmaram Pandurang was supported by prominent reformers like **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade** and **R.G. Bhandarkar**.
 
• The organization emphasized **monotheism**, promoting a belief in one God while rejecting idol worship and rituals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prarthana Samaj:**

 
 
• The term "Prarthana" means prayer. The organization focused on **spiritual upliftment** and ethical teachings.
 
• It worked towards the **upliftment of women** and advocated for their education and rights.
 
• The Samaj was influenced by the **teachings of the Upanishads** and reformist ideas of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
 
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang:**
 
 
• He was a physician by profession and a leading social reformer in Maharashtra.
 
• He played a key role in initiating reform movements that addressed **superstitious beliefs** and social evils.
 
 
 
• **Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade:**
 
 
• Ranade was a prominent figure in the Prarthana Samaj and supported its reformist agenda.
 
• He emphasized the importance of education and economic development in social progress.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of goods that a person can be excluded from enjoying its benefits?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Private goods** are goods that are excludable, meaning individuals can be prevented from using them if they do not pay.
 
• Private goods are also **rivalrous**, as one person's consumption reduces the availability for others.
 
• Examples of private goods include food, clothing, cars, and housing.
 
• These goods are primarily provided through markets and are subject to the forces of supply and demand.
 
• Private goods contrast with public goods, which are non-excludable and non-rivalrous.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Goods**

 
 
• These are goods that are non-excludable (cannot prevent usage) and non-rivalrous (usage by one does not reduce availability to others).
 
• Examples include national defense, street lighting, and public parks.
 
• Public goods are often provided by governments due to market failure in supplying them adequately.
 
 
 
• **Merit Goods**
 
 
• These are goods that the government believes individuals undervalue and under-consume, such as education and healthcare.
 
• Merit goods are often subsidized or provided for free by the government.
 
 
 
• **Free Rider Problem**
 
 
• Occurs when individuals benefit from resources, goods, or services without paying for them.
 
• This is a common issue with public goods as people cannot be excluded from usage.
 
 
 
• **Excludability**
 
 
• A property of goods where access can be restricted to paying consumers.
 
• Private goods are excludable, while public goods are not.

• **Iron Overload Causes:** Common causes include repeated blood transfusions, excessive dietary iron, and certain hereditary conditions.
 
• **Symptoms of Iron Overload:** Fatigue, joint pain, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, organ dysfunction (e.g., liver or heart).

• This process primarily occurs due to the **heat energy from the Sun**, which provides sufficient energy for water molecules to escape into the atmosphere.
 
• Evaporation is a crucial part of the **water cycle**, enabling the movement of water from Earth's surface to the atmosphere.
 
• It mainly takes place over large water bodies such as **oceans, lakes, and rivers**, but can also occur on moist surfaces like soil and plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Cycle:**

 
 
• The water cycle, also known as the **hydrological cycle**, describes the continuous movement of water within the Earth and atmosphere.
 
• Key processes include **evaporation**, **condensation**, **precipitation**, and **runoff**.
 
• This cycle is essential for maintaining Earth's water balance and supporting life.

⇒ First perfectly divisible number = 1163 − 15 = 1148

⇒ Second perfectly divisible number = 2214 − 82 = 2132

⇒ Prime factorization of 1148 = 2 × 2 × 7 × 41 = 2² × 7 × 41

⇒ Prime factorization of 2132 = 2 × 2 × 13 × 41 = 2² × 13 × 41

⇒ Extracting the common prime factors with the lowest powers:

⇒ HCF = 2² × 41

For any two numbers, the product of their LCM and HCF is always equal to the product of the numbers themselves: LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b.

The HCF of a set of fractions is determined by finding the HCF of their numerators and dividing it by the LCM of their denominators.

questions.question: The smallest natural number which is divisible by 5, 10, 49 and 28 is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The smallest natural number divisible by a given set of numbers is their LCM.

Given numbers: 5, 10, 49, 28.

Identify the highest power of prime factors present in these numbers: 2² (from 28), 5¹ (from 5 or 10), and 7² (from 49).

LCM = 2² × 5¹ × 7² = 4 × 5 × 49 = 980

**∴ The correct answer is 980.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 5, 10, 49, and 28.

**Formula Used:**

Smallest divisible number = Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given numbers.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 5 = 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 10 = 2 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 49 = 7 × 7 = 7²

⇒ Prime factorization of 28 = 2 × 2 × 7 = 2² × 7

⇒ To find the LCM, we take the highest power of each distinct prime factor present in all the factorizations.

⇒ The distinct prime factors are 2, 5, and 7.

⇒ Highest power of 2 is 2²

⇒ Highest power of 5 is 5¹

⇒ Highest power of 7 is 7²

⇒ LCM = 2² × 5¹ × 7²

⇒ LCM = 4 × 5 × 49

⇒ LCM = 20 × 49

⇒ LCM = 980

**∴ The correct answer is 980.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is computed by multiplying the highest powers of all prime factors involved.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest positive integer that divides each of the numbers without leaving a remainder. It is formed by multiplying the lowest powers of only the common prime factors.

Relationship between LCM and HCF

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b', the product of the numbers is strictly equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. The formula is: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).
</p
